cells.Title: Compression exemption list and fresh archive storage
cells.Detail: The already-compressed extension list has one definition, shared by compression decisions and audit exemptions, and its published documentation agrees with it. Office/text formats are not exempt. Neither .iso, a filesystem container rather than proof of compression, nor the unconfirmed .mca, .bin, .dng and .pdf formats are exempt; sampling determines their compressibility. The list is a known-format fast path, not an exhaustive classification. Its answer is an input to the measured decision in LLR-086 and decides alone in mode off and below 256 KiB. Compressed output is a fresh .7z archive with .7z appended to the stored name and Compressed agreeing with that form. An existing unreferenced destination is removed before archive creation, so interrupted archives or orphaned content cannot be merged into the new archive. Compression effort defaults to 9 and follows FILEBACKUP_7Z_LEVEL (LLR-037); the resolved level and any rejected raw value are available to configuration validation without making restore depend on backup-only code.

cells.Title: Staging classification, reclaim and ownership fences
cells.Detail: On failure to create staging, logs the original error and classifies only an existing directory; otherwise rethrows the original error. Enumeration includes hidden entries, treats paths literally and refuses on errors. Empty and OwnerStale require a confirmation sample after at least 90 s, extended to the declared heartbeat cadence plus 30 s and capped at 600 s. Reclaim renames staging to Temp.stale-<utc>-<8 hex>, then rechecks the moved folder against the sampled identity; a live identity is moved back and refused. A failed move refuses without a retry loop. New staging receives its owner record immediately after creation. The aside folder is re-enumerated and only disposable exact-name leaves are deleted, followed by a non-recursive directory delete; unexpected content or any deletion failure preserves the folder and prints recovery guidance. OwnerLive, HoldsContent and PruneHeld refuse with [SR-075/owner-live], [SR-075/content-refused] and [SR-075/prune-held]; Indeterminate and a reparse-point staging directory use the content refusal. Successful acquisition returns the staging location and a retained heartbeat handle. All post-acquisition exits stop and drain the heartbeat without deleting data merely because work threw. Early cleanup proves the marker belongs to this run and that entries contain only its marker and disposable prior manifest, witness and directory-sidecar copies; it deletes those leaves with the marker last, then deletes the directory non-recursively. Doubt preserves staging and logs [SR-075/lock-lost], while retaining the original failure. Ownership is rechecked before staging-manifest publication, eviction, superseded-data preservation, backup-manifest/sidecar publication and finalization. Unreadable markers are retried three times about 300 ms apart; identity mismatches are not retried and abort without cleanup. The heartbeat is stopped and drained and its marker removed immediately before staging deletion or snapshot publication, so snapshots contain no live-run marker. Acquisition, classification, confirmation and reclaim occur under the staging OS lock; failure to obtain it refuses before touching staging. Holding that lock does not change owner-record classifications because older writers may not take it. Release occurs on early failure or after finalization, never before the publish rename completes.

cells.Detail: Planning identifies one re-home item per endangered (hash,length) key demanded by a surviving row with blank DataPath or an absent named file. Each item identifies the source path and row, destination folder/path/row, stored form and byte count. Destination is the backup root if it demands the key, otherwise the newest demanding snapshot. The content-addressed destination name equals the source DataPath. An infrastructure name or collision with a different existing file produces a code-2 problem; an identical existing file is a completed interrupted copy and permits resume. Re-home copies use literal paths and stage at '<destination>.fbprune.tmp'. Before publication, stored bytes match source length and hash; unless -SkipContentVerify, payload matches the row's xxH2Hash and Length, expanding archive content when required. The staged copy is then renamed into place. Only DataPath, Compressed and StoredAsHashSize in planned destination rows are changed. Each destination manifest is published through the shared manifest writer so its witness is regenerated; witnesses are never copied between folders.

cells.Detail: Prune preflight returns all refusals with code, kind and message, allowing -WhatIf to report them together and the batch to apply precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1. Code 2 covers a target that is not an existing direct-child dated Snapshot_ folder, wildcard names, malformed run state or populated backup without LastBackupRun, existing staging, plan name/collision problems, unreferenced target data unless -DiscardUnreferencedData, a broken pool or applicable storage-form disagreement, insufficient destination-volume capacity, and absent 7-Zip when compressed content needs verification. Capacity aggregates planned bytes by actual volume and skips unmeasurable volumes. Every pool manifest is witnessed: Mismatch/Malformed refuse with 3; Absent also refuses with 3 unless -AllowUnverifiedIndex. Pool proof with the target excluded reports every unresolved row and applicable form disagreement. Named-row form agreement expects .7z for Compressed=Yes and a non-.7z file for Compressed=No, exempting a source RelativePath ending .7z; blank-row comparison is gated as in LLR-054. Commit renames the target to Pruning_<name>, removing it atomically from all snapshot consumers, then deletes it. Before planning a name, committed residue cleanup deletes only Pruning_<that same name>, converts host failures to code 4, and never runs under -WhatIf. Uncommitted *.fbprune.tmp cleanup runs only inside the transaction after rails pass and staging is held; it scans pool folders and deletes a file only if that folder's own manifest does not reference it. A suffix alone never authorizes deleting user data. Sweep failures are code 4. Staging acquisition exclusively creates the directory and refuses an existing one with code 2, closing the gap after preflight; cleanup never deletes staging this invocation did not create. PRUNE.inprogress is published within the transaction.

cells.Detail: The content index maps (xxH2Hash,Length) to existing locations recording location type, folder, DataPath, full path, backup-root status and folder order. Each folder record holds folder, name, order, backup-root status and non-blank DataPaths in manifest order. By default each manifest is read once and discarded after indexing; whole row arrays are retained only when explicitly requested, keeping default retained memory O(stored objects), rather than O(rows of every snapshot). Prune, pool proof and form audit request whole rows; snapshot deduplication uses the lean index and re-reads only as specified in LLR-026. Snapshot discovery uses one shared dated-name grammar, sorts by name and parses dates while accepting _NNN collision suffixes. Inventory reports PhysicalBytes, BytesReclaimed and BytesReHomed using the same prune plan as actual deletion, so reported reclaim agrees with achievable reclaim. Location collections remain consumable on supported PowerShell versions.

cells.Detail: The form audit classifies stored bytes as Archive or Raw using the six-byte 7-Zip signature 37 7A BC AF 27 1C and compares that form with the filename and row flag. It scans the backup root followed by snapshots in name order and returns Folder, RelativePath, DataPath, Class, Observed, Expected and Repairable for NameLies, FlagOverRaw, FlagOverArchive, DanglingDataPath, BlankRowFormDisagreement and Unreferenced findings. A Compressed=No archive-shaped object's own bytes matching the row's (xxH2Hash,Length) are legitimate raw storage, regardless of source name. A .7z source extension is a cheap exemption. Non-Deep additionally exempts without hashing an archive-shaped, list-exempt source only when its stored extension equals its source extension and on-disk length equals the row's Length. This is a form check, not payload proof: equal-length substitutions can pass it. Other archive-shaped raw claims retain the confirming hash. Deep verifies payload identity and requires 7-Zip: raw bytes are checked by length and hash; archive-shaped content is first checked as the user's own raw archive and otherwise expanded and checked. Payload disagreement is reported. Repairs require evidence in the row's own folder, never re-pack, and change only stored name and Compressed while preserving six logical columns. Repairs group by folder and DataPath so each physical rename occurs once and all referencing rows follow it; payload-exempt rows retain their own Compressed value, with identity checked before renaming. Each changed manifest receives its own regenerated witness. Blank-row findings are report-only. Enumeration excludes infrastructure only at each folder root. Outcomes use SR-040; routine backup does not invoke the audit. Verify resolves paths read-only, creates no directories, needs no SourcePath and reports a missing backup root as code 2. After compression-policy changes, both forms of one key may exist; deduplication can leave a blank row whose recorded form disagrees with the surviving copy. That report-only finding is benign for restore because restore derives form from the located bytes.

The already-compressed-SOURCE exemption is keyed on the PAYLOAD, not on the file name (WP5 re-review residual HIGH): when the observed form is Archive while the row says Compressed=No, the file's OWN bytes are hashed against the row's (xxH2Hash,Length) - a match is correct raw storage of archive-shaped content and yields NO finding, only a mismatch is a genuine FlagOverArchive - because an already-compressed source can be named anything (archive.7z.bak, a .pack file, an installer payload).

cells.Detail: Free-space measurement resolves the path's containing volume on Windows and POSIX, returning unknown without throwing when measurement is unavailable. Volume identity comes from the actual mount table, choosing the longest enclosing mount point on a separator boundary with a containing-volume fallback; subdirectories on one volume share its identity. Restore uses the same measurement. Backup demand counts each new (hash,length) group not held by a non-blank backup row once at uncompressed Length, plus deduplicated staging bytes only when ChangePath is on a different volume from BackupPath. Demands sharing a volume are summed before comparison, since individually fitting demands can exceed capacity together. Preflight runs after diffing but before content writes and refuses insufficient capacity as a classified precondition failure. Refusal fails the set with entry-point status 1, writes none of this run's content and leaves no orphaned staging folder. Existing stored objects are not re-formed, so no migration demand exists. cells.Title: Blank-row healing and valid dedup adoption

Same-content healing does not stage superseded data.

cells.Title: Pool audit findings and kit-compatible form checks

Reserved device stems CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9 and LPT1-9 are refused in any case, with or without an extension. An invalid name is skipped before opening or hashing and reported with RelativePath and Reason. A mismatch deletes the destination and permits exactly one (hash,length) pool-recovery attempt, whose write is verified again. Recovery candidates are themselves verified, so a wrong-bytes candidate cannot qualify. A row that still cannot be recovered is ContentMismatch, a content-class failure (SR-040/SR-056). If content already proven by the locator mismatches after writing, it is WriteMismatch in the host class with no further search. A read-back failure is host-class and keeps the file. Each row is restored and verified at most twice.

cells.Detail: Source and pool walks include hidden files, dot-files and hidden directories, including external source-cache walks. cells.Detail: Every stored object is content-addressed. Each (hash,length) group elects the shortest RelativePath as owner, breaking ties ordinally; the owner's extension and the composed SR-081 decision define one physical form. The first successful write is reused by every subsequent member in the run. Storage-form selection is lazy, occurring only on first entry to the write path, and is memoized for the group even if a member's copy fails. Thus existing dedup hits and in-run twins never probe, and failed candidates cannot trigger repeated probes or warnings. No folder-tree storage mode or mirror-name refusal remains.

cells.Detail: Superseded-data preservation follows copy and eviction, since content-addressed writes do not overwrite prior objects. It preserves an old object in staging only when no row in the final manifest still claims that DataPath. Frozen rows and failed replacement rows retain their claims and bytes. If one content key has multiple physical names, an unclaimed twin may move to the newest snapshot but remains in the recovery pool; a final-manifest claim always retains its object.

Refuses a view root off the backup volume or overlapping any owned path in either direction. Independently refuses to wipe a view root containing anything other than generated view data. ConfigVersion=2 uses a closed key set. PreserveFolderTree is refused by name, rather than as a generic unknown key, in both JSON and CLIXML. BrowseView and ViewPath are accepted with their declared vocabulary, defaults and placement checks. CompressProbe accepts exactly lowercase off, excluded-extensions or always, defaults to always, survives default materialization and agrees across runtime validation, published schema, examples, help, field documentation and interface declaration. cells.Title: Forced browse-view action
cells.Detail: -Action View forces a browse-view rebuild and reports through the SR-040 status table, alongside the backup pipeline's own refresh.

Source directory enumeration includes hidden directories and emits RelativePath and Attributes for directories with no files beneath them or with a recorded attribute bit. Emptiness uses ancestors of already-enumerated file rows, avoiding repeated directory walks and keeping work linear in directories plus file rows. Unreadable directories are not claimed empty; non-portable directory names warn and are skipped without failing the set a second time. Recorded attributes are Hidden, System, ReadOnly and NotContentIndexed; unsupported or meaningless directory bits are excluded. Rows sort ordinally for byte-identical output on identical state. DIRECTORIES.csv is written beside the manifest after manifest publication, or removed when there are no rows. Staging retains the prior sidecar, never overwriting it from the current kit, so snapshots preserve their own directory state. Restore applies the advisory, unwitnessed sidecar last, after files are verified: creates directories parents-first, applies attributes deepest-first and refuses path traversal. POSIX restore creates directories and reports Windows attributes as inapplicable. Absent, unreadable or malformed sidecars never fail restore and leave ordinary file restoration unchanged.

Both restorers apply each row's own LastWriteTimeStr only after successful (hash,length) verification, including after recovery retries, so dedup twins do not inherit the stored owner's timestamp. Parsing accepts the round-trip timestamp; POSIX timestamp application retries without fractional seconds where necessary. Timestamp failure, including a blank or unparseable value, warns but leaves the verified row counted as restored. A read-only attribute does not prevent applying modification time.

Copy retries run in rounds, each trying every member of the content group, with delays of 250 ms then 1000 ms: at most three attempts and 1.25 s waiting per group. A destination that is a directory is non-transient and is not retried; other failures may be transient because a mistaken refusal loses a file whereas a mistaken retry costs time. Partial destination debris is cleared between rounds so retries do not merge into it. One retry budget is shared by all groups in a set, bounding delay on an unreadable tree; a standalone group call receives a fresh local budget. Exhaustion names the attempt count, states that the file is not in the backup, adds no new manifest row and marks the set failed. A prior-run row survives unchanged, preserving its already-stored bytes.

removed.text: The destination is cleared between rounds by the same Remove-Item the MIN-1 fallback uses, so a retry never lands on partial debris (and never merges into it, SR-004).

Covered at BOTH levels: the group-level cases build the group by hand and delete or lock the source, and an end-to-end case deletes a source file inside the real walk-to-copy window using a separate sniper process keyed on the step-5 source hash cache (the parent runspace is blocked on the backup child and cannot pump a FileSystemWatcher, which is why an in-process watcher never enters the window).

cells.Detail: Stored-form detection is restore-safe and derives form from bytes. No 7-Zip signature in the first six bytes means Raw. A signature with length unequal to the row's Length means Archive; with equal length, matching xxH2Hash means Raw because the user's archive itself is the payload, otherwise Archive. An unreadable object returns Raw so the copy attempt surfaces the actual I/O failure. Both restorers use this rule for resolved DataPath rows; recovered rows use the locator's proven form. Compressed remains in the nine-column schema only for the approximate capacity estimate, which warns when compressed rows exist.

notes: Current restorers support this byte-derived contract; LLR-050 and SR-050's named-path reliance on Compressed is stale.

cells.Detail: Base-57 encoding rejects values wider than the requested width rather than truncating. Decoding returns exactly the requested hexadecimal width, removes representation sign padding, restores leading zeros and rejects over-width fields. Stored names use '<hash22>_<len><ext>'. One canonical parser reads the first 22 characters, requires the separator at index 22, decodes base-57 length digits up to the first dot and preserves the remaining extension opaquely while rejecting path separators; malformed input returns no result without throwing. Current-grammar recognition is distinct from positive retired-grammar recognition: failure to match the current grammar does not by itself mark a damaged path as legacy. The bash restorer needs only the structural legacy predicate, matching the PowerShell legacy decisions, because recovery proves content rather than decoding names.

cells.Detail: The stored extension defaults to empty and accepts an empty string, so extensionless source files can be stored raw. The owner's extension is preserved verbatim and is not restricted to the base-57 alphabet; parsing preserves it byte-for-byte.

cells.Title: Portable size, temporary-directory and time operations
cells.Detail: POSIX file-size measurement selects a supported style once using a known regular file and requires numeric output, avoiding false success from an incompatible stat option; byte counting is the fallback. Temporary-directory creation uses an explicit template, and every caller checks success so an empty path cannot redirect writes to the filesystem root. Current-time formatting uses an explicit POSIX format. Modification-time fallback converts every ISO-8601 offset exactly using POSIX timezone semantics, whose sign is inverse: -06:00 becomes UTC+6:00. Failure warns rather than applying an incorrect time.

cells.Detail: Path canonicalization uses physical resolution where available; otherwise it refuses any '..' component instead of returning or lexically reducing an unresolved path. Lexical reduction is unsafe across links because kernel traversal can enter the protected backup even when a reduced string appears outside. Containment has three results: inside, outside and indeterminate. The target guard accepts only provably outside; destination traversal guards accept only provably inside. Every canonicalization failure, including advisory-directory containment, is handled without broadening access through an empty path.

cells.Title: Target prompt selection and dialogs
cells.Detail: Prompt selection is a side-effect-free decision from explicit session signals and returns None, Text or Gui. Interactive folder selection does not throw, supports Windows, macOS and Linux native folder dialogs, and safely marshals a Windows dialog to a single-threaded UI context when needed, without an unhandled background scripting failure. Bash folder selection is reached only through --pick-target and honors FILEBACKUP_PICKER as one quoted executable path, including spaces. Cancel or unavailable dialog leaves the target empty and produces usage with exit 2.

A junction or symlink into the backup therefore cannot make an inside target appear outside through lexical normalization. Both restorers enforce this physical containment.

cells.Detail: Staging ownership is backup-only and creates no restore dependency. After successful staging creation, an exclusive create publishes a once-only JSON owner record with SchemaVersion, Kind, fresh GUID RunId, set name, host, container id, boot id, pid, StartedUtc, HeartbeatIntervalSeconds and StaleAfterSeconds=1800. A collision aborts as lock-lost without touching another owner's state. Direct exclusive creation avoids check-then-rename races and leftover temporary markers. Marker reading tolerates concurrent heartbeat access and returns Parsed, ParseInvalid or Unreadable with record, last-write time and age where available. A fresh malformed record is OwnerLive and refuses, keeping a torn write safe. The classifier takes enumeration and marker evidence without performing I/O and returns Empty, EmptyFresh, OwnerStale, OwnerLive, PruneHeld, HoldsContent or Indeterminate; confirmation sampling belongs to the reclaim caller. The heartbeat runs independently of a blocked backup pipeline, performs one synchronous successful beat before starting periodic work, and remains retained for the entire ownership lifetime. A failed first beat throws because an unchanged timestamp could falsely classify a live owner as stale. Every beat verifies RunId and touches the same open file object, preventing a replacement between identity check and touch from refreshing a successor's marker. Stop is idempotent and non-throwing, cancels periodic work, drains in-flight callbacks and reports accumulated error count and last error; no touch lands after it returns. Reclaim classifies and confirms, renames staging aside without retry on failure, rechecks moved identity as in LLR-017, creates fresh staging and immediately publishes its owner record. Failure preserves the aside folder. Its re-enumeration includes hidden entries and refuses on errors; deletion removes only disposable exact-name leaves and the directory non-recursively, preserving unexpected content even if a resumed owner wrote between classification and rename. Ownership fences precede staging-manifest publication, eviction, superseded-data preservation, backup-manifest publication and finalization. A RunId mismatch aborts without cleanup; unreadable markers receive three retries about 300 ms apart. Holding the separate OS lock never changes a classification into reclaimable because an older writer may not participate.

cells.Detail: Compressibility sampling is backup-only and introduces no restore-kit dependency. Given a source path, default sample size 262144 bytes and three samples, it opens read-only; Windows sharing prevents sampling while a writer holds the file, whereas POSIX sharing is advisory. Length and modification time are checked before and after sampling; changes, inability to open, or any sampling I/O failure return unavailable without failing the run. Empty files also return unavailable. Below sample count × sample size, reads the whole file once as one sample; otherwise reads exact windows at offsets 0, floor((length-sample size)/2) and length-sample size, completing short reads until full or EOF. Each sample is compressed into a byte-counting sink and its count is taken only after encoder completion, avoiding underestimated incompressible output. The probe returns sampled and compressed totals and per-window ratios; random input does not measure below 0.98. The selected sample codec is Brotli at fastest effort: its history can detect 64 KiB-period repetition within a 256 KiB sample where a 32 KiB history cannot. Repetition beyond a window, such as a 1 MiB period, may be missed, costing space savings without compromising content. The pure decision accepts CompressEnabled, mode off|excluded-extensions|always, the extension-list opinion independent of the enable switch, length, minimum probe size, sample totals and savings threshold. It returns a compression boolean and one reason: CompressDisabled, ModeOff, BelowFloor, ListExempt, ProbeUnavailable, ProbeCompressible or ProbeIncompressible. Ordered decisions are: disabled means raw; off uses the list; below 262144 bytes uses the list; excluded-extensions exempts listed formats; unavailable measurement uses the list with one warning; otherwise compress only when aggregate compressed bytes are at most 90% of sampled bytes. No format-name override outranks measurement. The 0.10 savings threshold and 262144-byte floor are fixed defaults, not configuration keys. CompressProbe defaults to always. Decision and warning are memoized per group only when a write is needed, so dedup hits, in-run twins and existing objects never re-probe or change form. Sampling tries the owner then group candidates and uses the first available sample; only total unavailability falls back to the list. One DEBUG line per written group reports 'compress-decision: <rel> <Reason> ratio=<aggregate> windows=<r1,r2,r3>'. After successful writes, per-set physical-object counters report 'Probe stored raw: <n> objects, <bytes>', 'Probe compressed: <n>' and 'Probe reads: <bytes>'.

cells.Title: Atomic manifest publication
cells.Detail: Canonical manifest rows are written to MANIFEST.csv.tmp beside the destination after removing any stale temporary copy. An ordinary write or publication failure removes the partial temporary file and rethrows. A single atomic overwrite rename publishes the complete new manifest, then its witness is computed from the published bytes. A process kill therefore leaves a complete old or new manifest; a kill after rename but before witness publication leaves a stale witness that fails loudly (SR-038). Path resolution uses the caller's filesystem location consistently, including relative paths. Publication does not promise durable flush before rename: power loss can lose the newest write on a filesystem that reorders data and rename.

cells.Title: Temporary manifest exclusion and staging tolerance
cells.Detail: MANIFEST.csv.tmp and MANIFEST.csv.meta.tmp are root-level infrastructure in backup and snapshot folders, excluded from orphan scans, form audits, prune sweeps and recovery candidates. Staging classification ignores the exact case-sensitive MANIFEST.csv.tmp leaf before checking for unknown content: with an owner marker it follows that marker's OwnerStale/OwnerLive result, and alone it is Empty subject to directory age. Other unknown entries still mean HoldsContent. Reclaim and own-staging cleanup allow this temporary manifest as a disposable leaf and remove it by exact name before the marker. It is never the only copy of content; the authoritative manifest still exists beside the incomplete copy.

cells.Title: Atomic-publication kit compatibility
cells.Detail: Atomic manifest publication does not change restore semantics. Older kits restore the same stores without a kit refresh, because the changed manifest-writing capability is bundled but not used by restore. Both bundled restorers retain equal revision markers, and a bundled behavior change advances the revision even when restore logic itself is unchanged.

cells.Detail: The staging OS lock is located at <ChangeRoot>/Temp.lock. Acquisition opens or creates it read-only with exclusive sharing, so read-only file attributes do not prevent locking, and returns its path and a held lock handle. Any open exception receives at most three attempts 250 ms apart, then refuses with a message beginning [SR-075/lock-held]. Windows sharing errors 0x80070020/0x80070021 and would-block errors 11 on Linux or 35 on macOS select 'held by another process' wording; other errors say 'could not be opened', but all refuse identically. A lock-held refusal is distinct from a lost owner-marker lock. Release accepts an absent handle, is idempotent and non-throwing, clears the retained handle and never deletes the lock file. This capability is backup-only.

Backup resolves paths and creates missing roots, then acquires the staging OS lock before reading any store state. Failure appends one refusal line to backup.log without truncation, fails the set and returns because the live holder owns that log. Under the lock it reads the previous completion date, checks the populated-manifest-without-date guard and verifies the manifest witness, in that order, before initializing the log. Any such failure releases the lock and preserves the original error, including witness exit 3, and leaves the previous log intact. Logger-creation failure also releases and rethrows. Staging creation, classification, confirmation and reclaim all receive the held lock, but their owner-record decisions remain unchanged because older writers may not lock. An early staging failure releases it. Otherwise release occurs on every exit after stopping and draining the heartbeat, and on success only after staging finalization, run-state persistence, deduplication and browse-view work. The lock remains held throughout marker deletion and snapshot publish rename.

cells.Detail: Prune acquires the same staging OS lock once after root resolution and before the per-name loop, committed-residue cleanup, preflight, staging creation or re-homing. -WhatIf does not acquire it. Failure returns for every requested name Status=Refused, Code=2 and one staging-busy refusal with the [SR-075/lock-held] message. The entire batch holds the lock and releases it on all exits. Existing staging still refuses independently; staging is created exclusively and carries PRUNE.inprogress.

The staging OS lock file is never written, truncated or deleted. Snapshot, prune, audit, kit-refresh and restore discovery consider dated snapshot directories, while residue and staging operations address their exact directory names, so the persistent lock file is invisible to those consumers.

cells.Detail: Store repair and kit refresh acquire the same staging OS lock within the mutation operation itself, covering direct callers. A blank change root refuses; a missing one is created. Any lock failure logs one ERROR and throws with [SR-075/lock-held]. Repair locks before auditing so evidence and repair share one state; kit refresh locks before snapshot enumeration. Both skip locking under -WhatIf and release on every exit. The entry point maps lock failure to exit 2. Read-only Verify, Snapshots, View, Deep audit and both restorers do not acquire this lock: their writes are confined to the separate view root, scratch space or restore target. Other store-writing steps rely on invocation beneath the backup or prune lock; direct invocation of an exported step does not itself acquire a lock.
